rv.q: In any case, 'Salt' is a remarkable piece of theatre. It's taken two years for it to reach London and it's only here for a couple of weeks. If you can see it, do see it.
Delivered with consummate composure by Rose, it has the force of ritual.

She’s enacting an attempt to smash the weighty legacy of the Atlantic slave trade. The gesture is cathartic — the block splinters dramatically — but the evidence of the past can never be annihilated. In part this is a travelogue, recounting Thompson’s efforts to retrace Britain’s slaving routes.

Along with a filmmaker friend she made a boat trip from Britain to Ghana, then travelled to Jamaica, then back again. This show is the result of that trip, and part of Thompson’s wider project of exploring Black British identity.
